site.title: Commonplace
site.description: Essays, field guides and notes from the GTA and beyond.

posts.title: Chalk, Cue & the 401: A Field Guide to the Best Pool Halls in the GTA
posts.dek: Seven rooms worth the trip - from 35 Diamond tables in Scarborough to a 2 a.m. rack in Oakville - with addresses, rates, hours, transit and the unwritten rules nobody tells you before the break.
posts.author: Andrew

posts.title: One Fare, End to End: A Slow Rider's Guide to the 501 Queen
posts.dek: Twenty-odd kilometres of Queen Street from the Humber to the Beaches, seen at streetcar speed - how the line really works, three acts of window-seat city, the stops worth getting off for, and the small unwritten rules of riding the whole thing in one sitting.
posts.author: Andrew

posts.title: How to Keep a Commonplace Book (and Why It's Worth the Trouble)
posts.dek: The journal is named after an old, unfashionable habit: copying down anything worth returning to. What a commonplace book is, how to start one in ten minutes, and how to keep it from becoming another abandoned system.
posts.author: Andrew

posts.title: The Quiet Download: What Your ISP Sees When a Server Does the Torrenting
posts.dek: Two ways to pull the same 17 GB file across the internet - BitTorrent straight to your laptop, or a small cloud box that does the torrenting and hands you the finished file over HTTPS. The privacy difference has less to do with encryption than you'd think.
posts.author: Andrew
